name: Independent Congregational Church
description:
Independent Congregational Church
Congregationalists joined Presbyterians in organizing a church in 1836.  When a split occurred in 1883, they formed the Independent Congregational Church.  Chicago architect Joseph C. Llewellyn designed this Neo-classical church, built in 1907, to accommodate 800 people.  Weekly radio broadcasts of Sunday services, begun by Reverend Doctor Carleton Brooks Miller in 1930, continued into the twenty-first century.
